doc.title: Bley Carla — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Management with Thomas Stowsand and Ted Kurland
summary: Thomas Stowsand of Saudades in Austria managed her throughout, with Ted Kurland in the United States for ten years.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Managers, bookers and the business of getting work

blocks.x: Who did... who was involved in the management of it? Did you have any say in that or any...
Yeah. That was, I believe from the very beginning Thomas Stowsand.
Of Saudades, which is a company in Austria. And that was my only manager I think my whole career. He died now, but I still have Saudades.
Did you have any state-side representation where the band played?

Yes, I had Ted Kurland for ten years, but he never got me any gigs. But I didn’t want any gigs. I didn’t like to play in person. Once I got through the Jack Bruce stage and realized it was not gonna be what it was, rock and roll had that to speak for it. But Jazz had the worst hotel in town, and eating whatever band slop was given to you by the club owner, and losing a lot of money by having excess baggage. But after ten years it was better. We actually made some money. And Thomas Stowsand stayed with us until we did make money, and made him a lot of money too.
